subject: trekkies
one_liner: A continuity intelligence platform for organizations that need to establish, defensibly, who said what about which episode.
brand_voice_notes: Defense-contractor prose applied to a disagreement about a shuttlecraft. Never acknowledges that the stakes are low. Speaks of fans as subjects, of opinions as assertions, and of a Discord server as a records environment. The humour comes entirely from the gap between the seriousness of the apparatus and the triviality of what it is pointed at. No winking, no exclamation marks, no self-awareness.

hero.h1: Every claim about the show is a claim of record.
hero.sub: Canonry ingests thirty-one years of forum posts, panel recordings, convention floor audio and unlicensed episode guides into a single continuity graph. Your moderators stop arguing. They start citing.

features.title: Frame-level provenance
features.blurb: Every assertion is anchored to an episode, a timecode, a shooting draft and the individual who made it. Disputes that historically ran nine years now close in under four minutes, or escalate to a panel of three archivists who have never met your community and owe it nothing.

features.title: Canon drift detection
features.blurb: Continuous monitoring identifies the exact hour a community begins treating an invented detail as settled fact. Alerts fire at forty percent adoption. By sixty percent the platform stops asking and begins correcting the record on your behalf.

features.title: Subject integrity scoring
features.blurb: Each member of your community carries a rolling integrity score computed from citation accuracy, retraction latency, unsourced enthusiasm and known affiliations with rival continuities. Scores are visible to moderators, to the subject, and to anyone the subject has ever replied to.

pricing_tiers.name: Cadet
perks: No export, no print, no screenshot
Your queries are ingested as evidence

pricing_tiers.name: Registry
pricing_tiers.tagline: For communities with a moderation problem they have stopped describing as a moderation problem.
perks: Full continuity graph, all series, all drafts
Integrity scores pushed to your Discord hourly

pricing_tiers.name: Prime
pricing_tiers.tagline: For organizations that own the canon, or intend to.
perks: Retroactive amendment with no notice to affected subjects
Disputes resolved before they are filed
One dedicated archivist, on site, indefinitely

testimonials.quote: We had a nine-year disagreement about a shuttlecraft. Canonry closed it in an afternoon and then flagged four of our moderators.
testimonials.name: Denise Holloway
testimonials.title: Continuity Officer, Sector 12 Fan Coalition

testimonials.quote: My integrity score sat at 41 for two months. I have since retracted eleven posts, and the platform has restored me to 78. I do not dispute the original finding.
testimonials.name: Marcus Vance
testimonials.title: Panel Moderator (Provisional), Regional Convention Circuit

testimonials.quote: It identified the member of our server who had been inventing episodes. He had been doing it since 2011. Nobody had checked.
testimonials.name: Priya Raghunathan
testimonials.title: Volunteer Archivist, Deep Space Reference Working Group

demo_screen_concept: A continuity reader console styled as a microfilm carrel: a left rail of subject dossiers (community members with integrity scores, jurisdiction codes and dispute counts) filtered by class chips (ALL / FLAGGED / DRIFT / CLEARED); a centre frame viewer that loads the selected subject's archive portrait beside the flagged assertion, its citation chain, its drift percentage and its retraction latency; a right rail of contested assertions with a working FLAG FOR REVIEW toggle per row; a frame counter and roll advance control across the top; and a fake archive search that filters the subject rail live. Selecting a subject advances the frame, swaps the dossier, and recomputes the disputed-assertion list.

images.rationale: Hero skipped because the hero is a piece of film rather than a picture of one: the composition is a typographic frame lit by a CSS lamp pool, and a photograph in it would compete with the sprocket rails. Demo subject asset generated (1 of 4) because the demo is a subject-ID surveillance console and its centre panel is a dossier portrait, which is exactly photo-shaped; the remaining rail subjects keep the CSS reticle treatment. Testimonial headshots generated (3 of 4) because the landing page names three fictional subjects and a duotone personnel-file portrait is the whole joke of the tier. All four passed the vision judge on the first attempt; none dropped.

design_direction.style: Microfilm reader carrel, ground-glass amber dark mode. The page is staged as a roll of 16mm archival microfilm loaded into a reader by a data-intelligence company that has decided a fan's opinion is a primary source and a message board is a records series. One warm reader-hood black (#100E0A) runs the entire page with no light mode, no glass, no backdrop blur, no clay volume, no bento lattice, no felt panels, no foil bands, no banknote plates, no vellum scribe lines, no enamel keylines, no drafting grid, no wall labels and no moulded shells. Nothing on the page casts a shadow, because a projected image has no edge to cast one. In place of shadow the page has light: a single soft radial lamp pool (a radial-gradient of amber at 6 to 10 percent opacity, never higher, never animated) sitting behind the active surface, so content reads as illuminated from behind rather than raised above. Nothing has a border radius above 2px, because film frames are cut square. The organising move is the frame: every major section is a film frame, a full-width block hemmed left and right by a sprocket rail (a vertical repeating-linear-gradient of 14px bone perforations at 32px pitch, built in pure CSS, never an image) and opened by a header strip carrying a roll number, a frame counter and a records-series code in letterspaced mono, so sections arrive as exposures on a roll rather than as cards in a grid. The core motif is the reticle: two 1px bone hairlines crossing inside a 1px bone circle at 999px radius, the projected crosshair of a reader lens, used as the list bullet, the feature index, the pricing tier mark, the testimonial portrait frame and the section marker, so every discrete item on the page reads as something the lens has been aimed at. The second motif is the splice: a 12px horizontal band of 45-degree bone hatch with a 40px gap cut out of it where the frame count sits, hemming every section seam, marking the places where the roll was cut and taped. The third motif is the underexposed well: telemetry sits in recessed wells one step darker than the hood with a 1px amber hairline along the top edge only, so figures read as burned into the film rather than printed on a card. One lamp amber (#DDA83F) is the sole carrier: the wordmark, every headline accent, every sprocket, every reticle, every primary CTA and every frame rule, always as a flat flood or hairline with hood black knocked out of it. One rationed ultraviolet inspection blue (#6E86E8) is quarantined strictly to continuity-violation telemetry (uncited assertions, drift percentages, retraction latency, contested frames, flagged subjects, the withheld line in pricing) and appears nowhere decorative, so the only cold colour on a warm page is always the platform informing you that your memory is wrong. Bricolage Grotesque sets the wordmark and headlines at monumental sizes with the flat confidence of a vendor that does not describe what it sells, tracking tightened to -0.03em at display sizes and set flush left against the sprocket rail. Karla carries plain, faintly procurement-grade body copy at 17px with a 1.62 line-height and a 66-character measure. Every figure that pretends to be archive telemetry (roll numbers, frame counts, integrity scores, drift percentages, retraction latency in hours, stardates, tier prices) is set in Azeret Mono with tabular figures inside the underexposed wells, so it reads like the finding aid, not marketing. Photographs, where they exist, are duotoned into amber and hood black and framed by a reticle, so a person always arrives as a subject on file. No light mode, no glass, no blur, no neon, no scanlines across the whole page, no CRT curvature, no gradients on type, no clay shadow pairs, no offset sticker shadows, no bento lattice, no drafting hairline grids, no rubrication, no versals, no guilloche, no lathe rules, no leg bands, no chenille patches, no cartridges, no wall labels, no title blocks, no dimension lines, no split-flap numerals, no HUD corner brackets, no emoji. Reads like a company that files your favourite episode under 'records series' and considers your recollection of it a liability.
design_direction.archetype: Data-intelligence platform product page issued as a roll of archival microfilm: a lamp-lit hero frame carrying a monumental grotesque claim over an ingest telemetry strip in mono, three numbered feature frames indexed by reticles, three testimonial frames with reticle-framed duotone subject portraits and case file numbers, a three-tier access schedule laid out as a ruled records schedule rather than floating cards, a closing custody band, and a handoff to the continuity reader demo.
design_direction.motion_vocab: Film-transport restrained. Sprocket rails draw down from the top over 600ms once on reveal. Frames advance by translating up 6px on a 40ms stagger and never move again. The lamp pool fades from 0 to its fixed 8 percent over 700ms and holds. Reticles rotate one quarter turn over 240ms on hover and stop square. Primary CTAs invert to an amber flood with hood-black type knocked out and depress 1px on press. Blue violation counters step once on entering the viewport and then hold. Focus is a 2px amber ring offset 3px. No parallax, no looping animation, no glow pulses, all gated behind prefers-reduced-motion.
design_direction.hero_composition_notes: Full-bleed hood black with the lamp pool centred behind the headline block and falling off to nothing by the edges. Sprocket rails run the full viewport height at both margins from the first pixel, so the page reads as loaded film before a single word is read. A frame header strip sits above the headline carrying ROLL 0441 / FRAME 001 / SERIES TREK-C in letterspaced mono, with a bone hairline beneath it. Headline set flush left at clamp(2.9rem, 7vw, 5.6rem) in Bricolage Grotesque 800, tracking -0.03em, with one word flooded amber. Subhead in Karla at 17px held to a 60-character measure directly under it. Beneath that, a single-row ingest telemetry strip of four underexposed wells (posts ingested, subjects on file, assertions contested, mean retraction latency) with the contested figure in inspection blue. Two CTAs on one line: an amber flood primary to the demo, and a bone hairline secondary to the pricing schedule. No hero photograph, because the hero is a piece of film, not a picture of one.
